title: Chreode: A Cell World Model for One-Step Temporal Dynamics and Perturbation Prediction
domain: Single-cell developmental dynamics and genetic-perturbation prediction
dataset_or_cohort: Pretraining: seven public mouse embryonic datasets (tome-mouse, GSE140802, GSE115943, E-MTAB-6967, GSE106340, GSE132188, GSE275562); downstream: Weinreb hematopoiesis, Veres islet differentiation, Norman Perturb-seq, and CellStream appendix datasets
sample_scale: 2,477,217 pretraining cells across ten leaf trajectories, 88 sampled timepoints, and developmental times from 0 to 19 days; downstream task sample counts are dataset-specific
institution_count: Multiple public datasets and laboratories; exact aggregate institution count NI
split_strategy: All downstream datasets are held out from pretraining; task-specific train/test splits are shared across methods; Weinreb fate evaluation is clonally held out
observation_process: Population snapshots of single-cell gene expression across developmental time; counts are harmonized, library-size normalized to 10,000, log1p transformed, and encoded in a shared latent space
missingness: Gene vocabularies are restricted to 16,520 one-to-one mouse-human orthologs for cross-species transfer; no cell-level missingness analysis is reported
censoring_or_competing_events: NA for population-transition benchmarks; lineage fate is evaluated on clones with sufficient released annotations
state: A 128-dimensional scVI latent representation of cell state and its population distribution
observation_decoder: The frozen scVI decoder maps latent states toward gene-expression space; most headline transition metrics are computed in the shared latent space
action: Optional action token in the Waddington-DiT transition; it is null during developmental pretraining, while downstream perturbation transfer inserts the learned representation into GEARS for CRISPRi single-gene knockout prediction
action_provenance: Observed developmental time differences and labeled genetic perturbations from public single-cell datasets
transition_mechanism: A stochastic one-step Waddington-DiT residual transition conditioned on source state, elapsed time, and an optional action, with potential-gradient, antisymmetric-flow, and stochastic-spread components
maximum_horizon: One learned transition over a requested elapsed-time delta; evaluated from Weinreb day 2 to days 4 or 6 and from Veres t0 to seven later targets
rollout_regime: Single-pass population generation with 32 stochastic samples per source cell; no chained free-running multistep rollout
capability_claim: One-step future population prediction plus transferable cellular-dynamics representations for fate and perturbation tasks
baselines: Matched scratch Waddington-DiT, PI-SDE, PRESCIENT, identity/source replay, linear time-delta, scDiffEq, moscot, WOT, static-DiT, official GEARS, and scVI replacement
state_fidelity_metrics: Sinkhorn W2 in the standardized scVI latent, decoded gene-space analyses, MMD appendices, clonal-fate Pearson correlation, and DE20 gene-expression metrics
transition_metrics: Per-target Sinkhorn W2 for developmental transitions; masked fate Pearson correlation; DE20 MSE, correlation, and delta-correlation for perturbation transfer
rollout_stability: Long-delta behavior and architecture ablations are reported, but there is no recursive rollout-drift evaluation because inference is one step
action_sensitivity: Perturbation-transfer embedding replacements and action-conditioned architecture are evaluated; pretraining uses a null action and no dose-response or action-shuffle audit is reported
calibration_and_uncertainty: Stochastic samples are generated, but calibrated uncertainty, coverage, and predictive-interval evaluation are explicitly absent
external_validation: Evaluation uses multiple held-out public datasets and cross-species ortholog transfer; no adult-human-tissue, wet-lab, or clinical validation
decision_utility: Biological transition, fate, and perturbation-prediction benchmarks only; no experimental intervention-selection study
safety_evaluation: Broader-impact discussion is provided, but there is no wet-lab hazard, off-target, or downstream intervention-safety evaluation
statistical_analysis: Mean and standard deviation over three downstream seeds; matched data representations and splits; no formal hypothesis-test family is reported
causal_language: Uses action-conditioned and perturbation language without identifying an individual causal treatment effect
estimand: Distributional cell-state transition under observed developmental timing, plus predictive performance for labeled perturbation populations
confounding_strategy: scVI uses dataset identity as a technical batch covariate; no causal confounding adjustment
positivity_and_overlap: NI; perturbation and developmental support are restricted to observed datasets and the shared ortholog vocabulary
counterfactual_validation: No ground-truth individual counterfactual validation; comparisons use observed target populations
code_access: An anonymized code artifact is reported in the paper, but no resolvable repository link was verified in the arXiv HTML
data_access: Public accession identifiers and licenses are listed for pretraining and downstream datasets
preprocessing_reproducibility: Detailed gene harmonization, normalization, latent model, optimizer, task protocols, metrics, and dataset accessions are reported
randomness: Three seeds control downstream splits and evaluation-noise draws; the pretrained backbone is one checkpoint with 32 stochastic samples per source cell
evidence_anchors: Sec. 3-4 for state and transition construction; Sec. 5 and Tables 1-4 for held-out tasks and metrics; Sec. 7 and Appendix I for scope; Appendix A.4 for seeds and metric definitions; Appendix E and reproducibility checklist for data and artifact claims
appraisal_strengths: Large multisource pretraining corpus, held-out downstream datasets, matched-architecture scratch control, explicit time conditioning, and separate temporal, fate, and perturbation evaluations
appraisal_limitations: One-step rather than recursive rollout; time-transition tasks require fine-tuning; perturbation transfer reuses GEARS; evaluation is largely latent-space; no calibrated uncertainty, adult-human pretraining, wet-lab validation, or causal identification
source_status: Primary arXiv v1 HTML inspected on 2026-09-12; open access

title: Clin-JEPA: A Multi-Phase Co-Training Framework for Joint-Embedding Predictive Pretraining on EHR Patient Trajectories
domain: ICU electronic-health-record trajectory modeling and clinical risk representation learning
dataset_or_cohort: MIMIC-IV ICU stays with hourly observations, interventions, and admission demographics
sample_scale: 84,497 ICU stays from 64,874 patients; approximately 197,000 overlapping training windows
split_strategy: Patient-level 70/15/15 train/validation/test split; stays longer than 72 hours yield overlapping windows with a 12-hour stride
observation_process: Original-order vital signs, laboratory values, severity scores, medications, ventilator settings, and procedures are serialized as structured natural-language text in one-hour bins
missingness: No value imputation or normalization; unobserved readings are absent from the hourly state text and repeated measurements retain their original order
censoring_or_competing_events: Trajectory windows are capped at 72 hours; no time-to-event censoring or competing-event analysis
state: A Qwen3-8B encoder with frozen base weights and LoRA adapters maps state, action, and demographics text separately into 4,096-dimensional embeddings
observation_decoder: No decoder to clinical measurements; future states remain latent and are pooled with history for shallow downstream probes
action: Hourly text describing active clinical interventions and doses
action_provenance: Observed interventions recorded in MIMIC-IV; no evaluated alternative treatment policy
transition_mechanism: A roughly 92-million-parameter block-causal Transformer predicts the next continuous latent state from demographics and prior state-action embeddings
maximum_horizon: 48-hour evaluated autoregressive rollout after a 24-hour context within a maximum 72-hour window
rollout_regime: Deterministic free-running latent rollout; each predicted embedding is fed back as the next state input
capability_claim: Action-aware latent patient-trajectory simulation and reusable representation learning, without validated alternative-intervention response
baselines: V-JEPA 2-AC-style training, SFT-only encoder, curriculum ablations, Ridge, LightGBM, LSTM, and TCN
state_fidelity_metrics: Encoder output variance for collapse, latent cohort displacement, and downstream AUROC/AUPRC across 15 tasks
transition_metrics: Normalized L1 distance between autoregressive predicted latents and encoded future latents across a 48-hour horizon
rollout_stability: Horizon-resolved drift with IQR bands; Clin-JEPA decreases 15.7% from its first-step normalized error while ablations and alternative paradigms are flat or diverge
action_sensitivity: NI; actions are input to the predictor, but no action replacement, shuffling, or dose-response experiment is reported
calibration_and_uncertainty: NI; the rollout is a deterministic conditional mean and no calibration or predictive-interval analysis is reported
external_validation: None; all pretraining, rollout, and downstream evaluation use MIMIC-IV
decision_utility: Downstream early-event and stay-level risk prediction with shallow probes; no treatment decision-impact or prospective study
statistical_analysis: IQR summarizes heavy-tailed rollout drift; downstream appendices report 95% bootstrap confidence intervals, but independent training-run uncertainty is unclear
causal_language: Describes patient dynamics and proposed action sequences without a causal estimand or treatment-effect identification
estimand: Prediction of future latent EHR states and downstream outcomes under the observational MIMIC-IV trajectory distribution
positivity_and_overlap: NI; support for intervention sequences is not audited
counterfactual_validation: None; no altered-action ground truth is evaluated
code_access: Public GitHub repository linked in the primary text
preprocessing_reproducibility: Hourly serialization, inclusion rules, source tables, feature inventory, architecture, and training curriculum are described in the paper and appendix
randomness: Exact model-training seeds and number of independent full training runs NI
evidence_anchors: Sec. 3.1-3.2 for state, action, and rollout; Sec. 5.1 for cohort and split; Sec. 5.2 and Fig. 2 for drift; Sec. 5.4 and Fig. 4 for downstream tasks; Appendix A for eligibility and features
appraisal_strengths: Patient-level separation, explicit free-running 48-hour latent rollout, curriculum failure-mode ablations, retained-predictor evaluation, and broad downstream task coverage
appraisal_limitations: Single database; latent predictions are not decoded to physiological values; no action perturbation, calibration, external validation, causal identification, safety analysis, or prospective utility evaluation
source_status: Primary arXiv v2 HTML inspected on 2026-09-12; open access

title: DRIFT: Direct-Recursive Intervention-Conditioned Forecasting of ICU Physiological Trajectories
dataset_or_cohort: MIMIC-IV v3.1 development benchmark and independently processed eICU-CRD v2.0 replication cohort
sample_scale: MIMIC-IV: 28,210 train, 6,045 validation, and 6,046 test stays; eICU-CRD: 38,633 train, 8,115 validation, and 8,345 test stays
institution_count: One MIMIC source plus a multicentre eICU database; all eICU test hospitals and hospital-ward pairs also occur in training, and the exact aggregate site count is NI in the core protocol
split_strategy: Patient-disjoint splits within each database; eICU preprocessing and training are independent of MIMIC, with a frozen test-evaluation protocol but no site holdout or weight transfer
observation_process: Twenty-seven physiological variables are represented hourly over the first 72 ICU hours with measurement masks and elapsed-time features
missingness: Earlier same-stay values are carried forward; leading gaps use training-set medians; masks and elapsed times are retained
censoring_or_competing_events: No event-time estimand; integrated analyses use a fixed 48-hour-eligible cohort
state: A direct Temporal Fusion Transformer anchor plus an auxiliary recurrent latent state and local mask-decay GRU hemodynamic correction
observation_decoder: One shared decoder predicts 27 physiological variables; a local branch refines heart rate and three blood-pressure variables
action: Hourly binary exposure to any of five vasopressors
action_provenance: Recorded treatment paths plus fixed donor-path substitutions constructed within exact time-mask and transition-mask strata
transition_mechanism: A one-hour action-conditioned recursive transition is aligned to direct states by stop-gradient distillation; a bounded low-dimensional discrepancy can correct the direct forecast
maximum_horizon: 48 hours, with endpoints at 8, 24, and 48 hours
rollout_regime: Recursive latent transition under a supplied future action path, used only as a bounded correction to the directly decoded trajectory rather than as an independently decoded free-running simulator
capability_claim: Recorded-path action-conditioned forecasting and measured input dependence, not valid alternative-treatment simulation
baselines: Persistence, GRU-action, Transformer-action, mask-decay GRU, TFT-action, TFT without dynamic action, capacity-matched TFT-Large, forecast-loss-transfer TFT-Large-FL, DirRecMO-8, and eICU-only PatchTST-action and iTransformer-action
state_fidelity_metrics: Normalized endpoint MSE across 27 variables and MAP mean absolute error; observed-only and integrated trajectory summaries
transition_metrics: Terminal-hour and integrated forecast errors across 8-, 24-, and 48-hour horizons
rollout_stability: Horizon-resolved results, residual-budget sensitivity, common 48-hour cohort analyses, and cross-database replication
action_sensitivity: Five donor mappings, full-stream and future-only path replacement, changed-window analysis, shifted-minus-recorded action gaps, and temporal alignment to first path divergence
calibration_and_uncertainty: No predictive calibration or interval-coverage evaluation; predictive uncertainty is identified as future work
external_validation: Cross-database replication on eICU uses independent training and a protocol locked before test evaluation; it is not model transport and is not site-held-out
decision_utility: No treatment recommendation, prospective decision-impact, or clinical-benefit evaluation
safety_evaluation: None beyond conservative interpretation and data-governance controls
statistical_analysis: Three seeds (42, 43, 44); 2,000 hierarchical bootstrap samples for primary paired analyses; 5,000 for the changed-window audit; plus-one two-sided probabilities and Benjamini-Hochberg correction within prespecified families
causal_language: Explicitly states that retrospective action-path results do not establish causal treatment effects
estimand: Recorded-path forecast error and an action gap measuring model input dependence when supplied vasopressor paths are replaced
confounding_strategy: Donors are matched only within mask strata without physiology, outcomes, severity, diagnoses, or model error; no treatment-effect confounding adjustment
positivity_and_overlap: Sparse action paths and many unchanged all-zero replacements are reported; formal treatment overlap is not established
counterfactual_validation: No; shifted actions retain the observed recipient outcome, which may be incompatible with the donor path
code_access: A public implementation is promised upon publication but was not yet available in the inspected primary text
data_access: MIMIC-IV and eICU-CRD require credentialed PhysioNet access; restricted patient-level artifacts are not redistributed
preprocessing_reproducibility: Detailed cohort, source-specific mappings, missingness handling, action reconstruction, model controls, estimands, and auditing procedures are documented
randomness: Seeds 42, 43, and 44; shared cohorts and paired bootstrap procedures
evidence_anchors: Sec. 3 for architecture; Sec. 4.2-4.4 for cohorts, metrics, and action replacement; Sec. 5 and Table 1 for results; Sec. 6 for evidence limits; Appendices B-D and H for preprocessing, perturbation, and replication; Appendix G.1 for governance and code status
appraisal_strengths: Patient-disjoint multicohort evaluation, capacity controls, explicit action-path perturbation, temporal divergence audit, prespecified paired inference, and unusually clear noncausal interpretation
appraisal_limitations: Forecast gains are small and concentrated on MAP; actions are binary vasopressor exposure without dose or co-interventions; eICU is not site-held-out; no calibrated uncertainty, causal identification, alternative-outcome validation, clinical utility, or public code at inspection
source_status: Primary arXiv v1 HTML inspected on 2026-09-12; open access

title: Model-based reinforcement learning for ultrasound-driven autonomous microrobots.
domain: Ultrasound-actuated biomedical microrobot navigation in artificial vascular microfluidic environments
dataset_or_cohort: Generated Pygame simulation data and physical camera trajectories from racetrack, circuitous, multi-output, vascular, mixed, randomized, static-flow, and dynamic-flow environments
sample_scale: No human or animal cohort; simulation policies are summarized over final 50 episodes, while physical experiments include up to hundreds of thousands of interaction steps and adaptation periods from 30 minutes to 10 days; exact independent microrobot and trial counts are NI
split_strategy: Training across several channel geometries with tests on new or randomized channels and subsequent fine-tuning; no conventional fixed train/validation/test split
observation_process: Camera images at 6-18 frames per second are resized, cropped, segmented, morphologically filtered, and tracked to recover microrobot and target position
missingness: A rescue routine uses the last observed coordinates and reverses recent actions when the microrobot leaves the field of view; no formal missing-data analysis
state: Processed image features plus current microrobot and target coordinates, encoded into the Dreamer v3 recurrent latent state
observation_decoder: The Dreamer decoder reconstructs observations and predicts rewards and latent dynamics for imagined policy learning
action: Selection of piezoelectric transducer activation, ultrasound frequency, and amplitude, represented with discrete or continuous controls depending on the experiment
action_provenance: Policy-generated actions during simulated and physical closed-loop interaction
transition_mechanism: Dreamer v3 recurrent state-space world model with deterministic recurrent state, stochastic latent state, observation reconstruction, reward prediction, and latent imagination
maximum_horizon: Multistep latent imagination; the exact imagination horizon is NI in the main text
rollout_regime: Free-running imagined trajectories train actor-critic networks; physical deployment is closed loop with new camera feedback and online adaptation
capability_claim: Closed-loop model-based planning and control of ultrasound-driven microrobots
baselines: Hyperparameter-tuned PPO, simulation-only and physical-only training conditions, reward functions, frame-skipping settings, training ratios, action-space variants, and unseen-environment adaptation
state_fidelity_metrics: Observation reconstruction is part of training, but no held-out image-fidelity or latent-state accuracy metric is reported
transition_metrics: Control reward, convergence steps, target-achievement rate, collision behavior, trajectory and timing measures; no direct held-out transition prediction metric
rollout_stability: Learning curves across six simulated geometries, physical transfer, unseen-channel generalization, randomized environments, and static or dynamic flow
action_sensitivity: Reward-function, frame-skipping, training-ratio, action-space, frequency, amplitude, wall-adherence, and flow-control variations
external_validation: Tests include unseen artificial channel geometries and physical transfer, but no in-vivo animal, patient, external laboratory, or clinical validation
decision_utility: Physical closed-loop target navigation reaches roughly 90% success after simulation pretraining and limited fine-tuning; this is a robot-control outcome rather than a patient outcome
safety_evaluation: Collision avoidance, wall-contact penalties, low-drag wall navigation, and a recovery routine are tested; biological injury, tissue damage, acoustic exposure, and in-vivo hazard outcomes are not evaluated
statistical_analysis: Descriptive exponentially weighted moving averages, rolling standard deviations, IQR boxplots, and final-50-episode distributions; no formal inferential comparison or independent-laboratory replication
causal_language: Physical action-response control language without a clinical causal estimand
estimand: Policy performance and sample efficiency under learned simulated and physical microrobot dynamics
confounding_strategy: NA for randomized policy interaction; no causal treatment analysis
positivity_and_overlap: Action support is limited to tested transducer-frequency-amplitude ranges; no formal support analysis
counterfactual_validation: Alternative actions are explored through control, but no causal counterfactual ground truth is defined
code_access: Public GitHub source and archived Zenodo release
weights_access: Trained checkpoints are publicly deposited with simulation and physical training data on Figshare
data_access: Generated training data, reward trajectories, success rates, checkpoints, and processed physical experiment CSV files are publicly available
preprocessing_reproducibility: Image pipeline, simulator, reward definitions, action controls, training settings, code, and processed data are documented and released
randomness: Exact random seeds and number of independent physical repetitions are NI
evidence_anchors: Fig. 2 and Methods for state, action, and world model; Figs. 3-6 for convergence, physical transfer, new environments, and flow; Discussion for scope; Data and Code Availability for artifacts
appraisal_strengths: Direct closed-loop physical control, simulation-to-real transfer, unseen-environment adaptation, dynamic-flow testing, model-free baseline, and strong code-data-checkpoint availability
appraisal_limitations: Artificial channels and microbubble clusters rather than in-vivo treatment; simulator omits important microrobot physics; exact replication counts are unclear; no direct transition-fidelity, calibration, biological safety, external-lab, or clinical outcome evaluation
source_status: Primary Nature Machine Intelligence full text inspected on 2026-09-12; open web access

title: Towards Surgical World-Action Modeling: A Preliminary Joint Visual-Trajectory Forecasting for Surgical Motion Planning
domain: Robot-assisted surgical video and instrument-trajectory forecasting
dataset_or_cohort: SurgWMBench constructed from SAR-RARP50 real clinical videos of robot-assisted radical prostatectomy
sample_scale: 1,637 suturing motion segments, 32,740 annotated frames, and one manually annotated task-relevant 2D instrument anchor per frame
institution_count: Source-site count NI in the paper
split_strategy: Follows the SurgWMBench protocol; exact train/validation/test counts and patient-level separation are NI in the paper
observation_process: Each segment contains 20 frames and 2D trajectory points; the first five are history and the remaining fifteen are prediction targets
censoring_or_competing_events: NA for fixed surgical motion segments
state: Latent visual representations jointly encoded with historical 2D instrument-anchor trajectories
observation_decoder: Separate heads predict future visual latents and 2D trajectory points; a frozen decoder maps visual latents back to RGB frames
action: No exogenous intervention or robot command; future instrument motion is an observational trajectory target
action_provenance: Manually annotated tool-anchor trajectories from recorded clinical surgery videos
transition_mechanism: A temporal-spatial encoder with visual-state and trajectory heads predicts three-step chunks that are recursively fed back
maximum_horizon: Fifteen future frames or trajectory points in five successive three-step chunks
rollout_regime: Fully closed-loop chunked autoregression at validation and test; compared with a direct one-shot fifteen-step forecast
capability_claim: Passive joint visual-motion forecasting as a preliminary planning representation, not executable surgical control
baselines: Direct one-shot prediction under the same history-only protocol; no independent state-of-the-art forecasting architecture or control baseline
state_fidelity_metrics: PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS for decoded visual predictions
transition_metrics: Segment-resolved PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, average displacement error, and final displacement error
rollout_stability: Metrics are reported for five non-overlapping future segments and show progressive visual degradation and trajectory-error accumulation at later horizons
action_sensitivity: None; action conditioning is identified as future work
calibration_and_uncertainty: None; uncertainty modeling is identified as future work
external_validation: None; one benchmark derived from one source dataset
decision_utility: No planning policy, robot execution, surgeon decision impact, or clinical outcome evaluation
statistical_analysis: Single reported metric table without confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run variation
estimand: Future visual-state and 2D instrument-trajectory prediction under recorded surgical motion
code_access: A public anonymized repository provides additional qualitative results; training and evaluation code availability is NI
data_access: SurgWMBench and SAR-RARP50 are cited; access conditions are not restated in the paper
preprocessing_reproducibility: Model losses, optimizer, scheduled sampling, horizon protocol, and metrics are detailed, but exact data splits and complete training artifacts are unavailable
randomness: Seeds and number of independent training runs NI
evidence_anchors: Sec. 2 for joint representation and chunked rollout; Sec. 3.1 for SurgWMBench and horizon; Sec. 3.2 for training; Table 1 and Sec. 3.3-3.4 for horizon results; Sec. 4 for limitations
appraisal_strengths: Uses real clinical surgery video, evaluates fully closed-loop fifteen-step prediction, couples visual and motion outputs, and reports horizon-resolved drift in both modalities
appraisal_limitations: No true action input, planning policy, robot control, external dataset, strong architecture comparator, statistical uncertainty, calibration, safety analysis, or explicit patient-level split; performance degrades substantially at long horizons
source_status: Primary arXiv v1 HTML inspected on 2026-09-12; open access
